title: Indian Wedding Season Guide: November to February Outfit Planner
excerpt: An Indian wedding season guide for November to February: what to wear to haldi, mehendi, sangeet, wedding and reception, plus winter tips.
body:
Indian wedding season runs mostly from November to February, and most weddings have four or five functions, each with its own mood. Plan one outfit per function: bright and easy for haldi, playful for mehendi, twirl-ready for sangeet, rich for the wedding and polished for the reception. Here is a function-by-function planner, with tips for travelling and the cooler months.

## The function-by-function planner

Use this table as a starting point, then adjust to the family's theme and the venue.

| Function | Mood | Colours | Silhouette | Fabric |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Haldi | Fun, messy, daytime | Yellow, mint, white, peach | Simple kurta set you do not mind staining | Cotton |
| Mehendi | Playful, seated for hours | Green, pink, coral, multicolour prints | Kurta palazzo or short kurti with flared pants | Cotton, block print |
| Sangeet | Evening, dancing | Jewel tones, pastels with shine | Flared Anarkali or sequin set | Georgette, taffeta |
| Wedding | Traditional, formal | Red, pink, royal blue, gold accents | Anarkali or heavy suit set | Georgette, silk, taffeta |
| Reception | Glam, evening | Pastels, metallics, deep jewel tones | Sleek Anarkali or embellished suit | Taffeta, organza |

## Haldi and mehendi: easy, bright and practical

The haldi is about turmeric, laughter and getting a little messy. Wear something comfortable that can be washed afterwards. A cotton kurta set in yellow, mint or white works well. Our [Mint Green Hand Block Print Cotton Kurta Pant Dupatta Set](/products/mint-green-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-dupatta-set-with-hand-work-yoke/) is fresh, breathable and easy to move in.

At the mehendi, you will sit for a long time while henna is applied. Choose short or three-quarter sleeves so your hands and forearms stay free, and avoid heavy dupattas that drag across wet henna. Hand block printed cotton in greens, pinks and corals suits the cheerful mood, and you can browse more ideas in our [hand block print](/hand-block-print-kurta-sets/) collection.

## Sangeet: dress to dance

The sangeet is the night everyone dances, so movement matters most. A georgette or taffeta Anarkali opens beautifully when you spin, and sequins catch the stage lights. If you prefer something lighter, the [Violet Nyra Cut Sequin Embroidered Cotton Suit Set](/products/violet-nyra-cut-sequin-embroidered-cotton-3-piece-suit/) gives sparkle while staying breathable.

Pin your dupatta at the shoulder and waist, and carry flat juttis for the dance floor.

## The wedding and reception: go richer

For the main ceremony, traditional colours like red, pink, royal blue and deep green feel right. As a guest, avoid matching the bride exactly, which usually means skipping full bridal red unless the family invites it. The [Royal Blue Georgette Anarkali Suit Set](/products/royal-blue-georgette-anarkali-suit-gota-handwork-dupatta/) has handwork and a gota lace dupatta, rich enough for a ceremony without overshadowing anyone.

Receptions lean modern and glamorous. Soft pastels with metallic detail look elegant under evening lights, and the [Sage Green Taffeta Silk Gota Work Anarkali](/products/sage-green-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-sequin-organza-dupatta/) with its sequin organza dupatta is a graceful reception choice.

For more inspiration across every function, see our [wedding guest outfits](/indian-wedding-guest-outfits/) page.

## Dressing for November to February weather

Winter weddings bring cool mornings and chilly nights, especially in North India and for diaspora weddings in the UK, Canada and the US.

- **Layer a shawl.** A pashmina-style shawl over an Anarkali looks elegant and keeps you warm at outdoor pheras.
- **Thermals underneath.** Thin skin-tone thermals sit invisibly under kurta sets.
- **Richer fabrics.** Taffeta, silk and georgette feel more seasonal than sheer summer cottons for evening events.
- **Day versus night.** Daytime haldi and mehendi can stay in cotton; evening functions call for heavier fabrics.

## Planning and ordering timeline

Start planning four to six weeks before the first function if you are ordering from abroad. Ready sizes ship in 2 to 4 working days and made-to-measure pieces in 5 to 7 working days, with delivery usually taking about 5 to 10 business days. That leaves time for a small alteration if needed.

Make a simple checklist for each function: outfit, dupatta, jewellery, footwear and a backup safety pin kit. Try everything on at least a week before you travel, so any fitting issue can be sorted calmly rather than on the morning of the event.

## Frequently asked questions

**How many outfits do I need for an Indian wedding?**
Usually one per function, so four or five for a full wedding. You can re-style one suit with a different dupatta and jewellery to save packing space.

**What colours should a guest avoid at an Indian wedding?**
Avoid full bridal red unless the family says it is fine, and check with hosts about black or white, which some families prefer guests to skip.

**Is an Anarkali suitable for every function?**
It works beautifully for sangeet, wedding and reception. For haldi and mehendi, a simpler cotton kurta set is more practical.

**When should I order outfits for a December wedding?**
Order by early November so there is time for stitching, shipping and any alteration.
